queries: WITH type_avg AS (SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS avg_price FROM Products GROUP BY production_type_code HAVING AVG(unit_price) IS NOT NULL), baseline AS (SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS b FROM Products WHERE unit_price IS NOT NULL), kept AS (SELECT t.production_type_code, t.avg_price, bl.b FROM type_avg t JOIN baseline bl ON bl.b IS NOT NULL WHERE t.avg_price > bl.b), kept_mean AS (SELECT AVG(avg_price) AS m FROM kept) SELECT AVG(k.avg_price) AS avg_type_price, AVG(k.avg_price - k.b) AS avg_above_baseline, AVG(k.avg_price - km.m) AS avg_above_kept_mean FROM kept k CROSS JOIN kept_mean km WHERE k.avg_price > km.m

assumptions.assumption: Types whose prices are all NULL have no average and are excluded from the per-type averages (they cannot exceed the baseline anyway).
If no baseline exists (no non-null prices) or no type survives both filters, the query returns a single row of NULLs (aggregates over zero rows) rather than zero rows.

assumptions.assumption: Types whose products all have NULL unit_price have no average and are excluded from the type-level set.
If no types survive the filters, the query returns one row of NULLs (aggregates over zero rows); if the baseline is NULL, no types are kept so the result is also NULLs.
